## Problem

## Requirements

- Input: one string, `s`.
- Output the number of contiguous portions of `s` that read identically forward and backward. Count positions independently, so equal-looking substrings found at different locations each contribute to the result.


```
public int countPalindromicSubstrings(String s)
```

## Notes

- Boundary cases include an empty input, which produces `0`, and a one-letter input, which produces `1`.

## Preparation

- Trace `"aba"` manually: it has 4 palindromic substrings (`a`, `b`, `a`, `aba`).
- The challenge commonly numbered 647 covers the same task. The longest-palindromic-substring exercise commonly numbered 5 relies on the same core expansion pattern and is useful practice as well.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think about expanding around centers—each palindrome has a center that can be a single character or a pair of characters.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use two pointers to expand outward from each center and count all palindromic substrings found.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The time complexity should be O(n^2) in the worst case, but you can optimize to O(n) using Manacher's algorithm.

</details>
